drafts.title: Noticing a Trade-off Between World Knowledge and Problem-Solving in Newer Small LLMs—Anyone Else Seen This?
drafts.body:
I came across an archived Reddit post from May 2025 discussing an interesting pattern in smaller local LLMs. The author noticed that newer models like Qwen 3 and GLM-4-0414 tend to outperform older ones in coding and problem-solving tasks but show worse world knowledge, sometimes even lagging behind older, lower-benchmarking models.

This seems to suggest a trade-off where training data might be more focused on problem-solving content, reducing knowledge density. For example, Qwen 3 8B reportedly has poorer world knowledge than Llama 3.1 8B, despite better coding skills. Has anyone else observed this kind of trade-off in their experience? How do you balance choosing models for tasks that require both strong knowledge recall and problem-solving abilities?

drafts.title: World Knowledge vs. Problem Solving in Local LLMs: Are Training Data Shifts the Cause?
drafts.body:
An archived discussion from May 2025 raised a point about a potential trade-off in some newer smaller LLMs: improved coding and problem-solving but degraded world knowledge. The source author’s private tests showed models like Qwen 3 14B having much worse world knowledge than older models like Phi 4 or Gemma 3 12B, despite benchmark claims.

One hypothesis is that newer models’ training data emphasize problem-solving content over knowledge-dense material. Given this, how might we effectively evaluate or select models when both knowledge retention and problem-solving are important? Are there known strategies or benchmarks that can help clarify these trade-offs beyond what the author’s private tests reveal?
